html:
SMTO-EXE-0256 — This workflow's steps or changes aren't valid

GUID: c252c60b-0c89-5f5e-b2ec-564b2feb3b06
Slug: recipe-workflow-invalid
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: recipes

What happened

  • SMTO found something in this workflow it can't accept, such as a removed required step, steps in the wrong order, or a step running in a way the workflow doesn't allow. The change wasn't saved, or the step didn't run.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If you were editing the workflow, select Cancel, open it again with Edit, and make a smaller change. SMTO rejects edits that remove required steps or break the order that later steps depend on.
  2. If this happened while an older workflow was running, open its conversation and select Save to workflow on the original message, then select Save workflow. Older step-by-step workflows only allow their recorded steps, one at a time; a newly saved request runs as a normal task.
  3. Before running anything again, check in the conversation whether any step already made its change. Running the workflow again could repeat a change that already happened.

What success looks like

  • The workflow saves without an error, or a new run finishes in its conversation.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the workflow's name, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't keep rerunning the workflow; a step may already have made its change.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Workflow validation rejected the definition, edit or step: an invalid binding expression or pointer, broken dependency order, a removed mandatory step, a saved historical operation ID, an oversized definition, or a parallel or background tool used during a recorded workflow.

What this means

  • The workflow violates its closed graph or expression schema, dependency order, retained-identity rules, required-step protection, size bound or allowed execution surface. Workflow diagnostics do not execute steps or grant approval. Preserve the pinned definition, original receipts, completed effects and any uncertainty; all execution uses the existing authorization boundary.

Why this can happen

  • The workflow violates its closed graph or expression schema, dependency order, retained-identity rules, required-step protection, size bound or allowed execution surface.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the specific graph, binding or edit rejection and compare required steps and dependencies with the accepted artifact.

How to fix it

  • Find which check raised recipe.workflow_invalid (recipes/bindings.py, recorded_workflow.py graph and TargetPolicy checks, recorder.extract, store.apply_recipe_update, validation.validate with its 128 KiB size limit, or runtime.control_guard). Keep prior dependencies and non-optional steps in edits, remove transient IDs, or re-save the request as a saved-request workflow.
  • Correct the rejected workflow structure or edit, preserving required dependencies and mandatory steps.

Retry and execution caution

  • Review the workflow and its current run evidence before retrying.

How to verify the fix

  • Validation accepts the reviewed graph without removed mandatory steps, historical operation IDs or unsupported child execution.

What not to do

  • Never repeat a write whose effect remains unknown.

Technical notes

  • Workflow diagnostics do not execute steps or grant approval. Preserve the pinned definition, original receipts, completed effects and any uncertainty; all execution uses the existing authorization boundary.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
